title: Rabbit and the Saturday-night fish fries
summary: Dawson recalls guitarist Rabbit playing for small pay at fish fries, and the drinks and crowds there.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you know Rabbit that played guitar?

Yeah, Rabbit, yeah, Rabbit, he was, he wasn't much, but he was used to sing a whole lot, you know. Fake, you know, go around and play around with fish fries, you see. There's a lot of fish fries. Every Saturday night, you see, you see all around Cypress Street. All them people used to get fish fries and hang a red lamp out on the front. The gateway, a red lamp. That was fish fries. People would go in there and sit down and eat fish and drink beer and stuff, you know. And they had the old drinks, they called it gin and raspberry. The gin and raspberry, you know, they put the raspberry syrup in it, make it pink. And wine, all that kind of stuff. And that Rabbit used to go around and play at them fish fries, you know. Mm-hmm. And he'd give them, just pay them a dollar and a quarter at night, that's all he'd get, a dollar and a half. But just sing and play.
What's your grandma called him Rabbit? Yeah.

The people would get in there and dance by his, just do the guitar, you see. Singing and playing the guitar, you know. He could sing to you, you know. And, uh, they'd be packed in the house, we'd be packed in the house party, you know. Fish fries, just like a house like this. Sometimes three rooms full of people. And people used to make money off their fish fries, too.
He made a good record, too, I tell you that. Yeah? I got a good record now. A rabbit?
Yeah. You see, you've been operating a long time, then. The rabbit's been dead a long time.
Well, I found the old record. Oh, I see.
